The game is really fun, but it's a bit frustrating how it feels like you're set up to fail. Winning in a single run is nearly impossible. I get that it's a "roguelite" — you're supposed to die, slowly unlocking shortcuts to make future runs easier and eventually reach the endgame. The idea is that the more enemies you kill, the harder the run gets. But something about that mechanic feels off. The most enjoyable part of the game, for me, is when enemies are tough but still beatable. That’s when the game feels the most intense and rewarding. Unfortunately, that sweet spot doesn't last long. Soon after, enemies start dealing way too much damage while you barely scratch them, and it kills the fun. Each run is mainly about unlocking shortcuts for the next one — that’s how progression works. I just wish it was designed a bit differently: more intensity, but less of those unfair, near-impossible fights. That said, the game has a lot of potential. It’s still in Early Access, so a few small issues are expected. Overall, it’s a solid experience — I’d give it 4 out of 5 stars.

游戏底子还是不错的，但是这游戏有些问题： 1、英雄技能太少了，各职业之间技能还是通用的，没有独特职业技能。 2、远程怪和投掷怪有点恶心了，特别是对于近战英雄来说，很难躲避。 3、有些地形进入后封锁了，必须杀完怪才能打开，在那么狭小的空间，还有不少范围攻击的怪，属于是难躲。 4、技能升满级以后，人物升级变得意义不大，后期打怪很吃力，怪在变强，但是人物基本没有变强。 5、有些地形确实要绕很远才能打开门，而且因为视角不能切换，看不到通道，能不能最好至少加个地图。 6、打击感的问题，攻击时怪物基本没有受击感，需要优化下。 总之，这里面很多问题都是因为需要解锁，不解锁前技能少，伤害低，强迫玩家必须通过不断刷刷刷来提升。很多类肉鸽也有局外成长，但是前提是玩家初始就有方法通关，而且不是必须通过刷刷刷解锁才能通关。

For the record, this game is great. But I'm here because I wanted to throw out a big PSA: Don't! touch the rosebush (thorn thing) unless you have a lot of healing. Otherwise you'll ruin your run like i just did. That thing did 5hp ticks/ second permanently. Might have been even more, either way, it killed me quickly and I had a great build going. 35 minutes down the drain, I'm kinda pissed that there's not an explicit warning about what it does because IT WILL ruin most runs. That said the game is great. I've enjoyed all the unlocks and am honestly surprised how much content there is. It started off rough, but once you start unlocking stuff you'll get stronger and stronger. Pretty much endless replayability and the game isn't even finished yet, nor have I unlocked all the areas, abilities, and skills. As soon as I think I've found everything there's something new and interesting. Highly recommended if you like roguelites. I've never even been a big roguelite person, but this one is so good. My only gripe would be the difficulty. It's extremely tough even after figuring out what works and what doesn't. Could just be bad at the game, but yeah I've died many many many times. Even full tank builds can get killed in an instant once you reach a new stage with stronger enemies.

类魂小品，可以玩但是没有看起来那么好玩，感觉像在玩DEMO。 优点： 1.关卡设计有点魂的意思，场景探索有点意思。 缺点： 1.糟糕技能命中判定。你的远程攻击经常会被场景挡住，移动也经常会被场景卡住，而这个游戏又特别喜欢设计一些狭小场景的战斗和高低差的场景，进一步放大了这些缺点。 2.令人迷惑的成长曲线。这游戏设计了一个名叫信仰负重的系统，杀的怪越多敌人越强。打怪同时具有正收益和负收益。一开始打怪升级是越打越强的，但是当你来到10多级的时候，升级的收益会边际递减，但敌人的增强却越不会递减，这时候你再打怪就是负收益，进入一个敌人越来越强但你自身不再成长的死循环，间接强制你死亡重开。 3.重复性太强。每个职业的核心技能基本就那么几个，基本是必拿的，装备词条也没法给你的战斗风格带来质变，BUILD玩不出什么花样。为数不多的技能里还有几个手感特别差的。点名战士的转转斧，那个旋转半径刚好卡在一个你近战打不到怪，远程又不安全的尴尬距，玩了一局战士再也不想玩了。

Remove dying from fall damage and this changes to a positive review. I get the desire to be similar to Dark Souls, but this is a Roguelite, and Dark Souls isn't. Other than that, phenomenal game.

Let me start this by saying I love the game, but would not recommend it to most people. I will recommend it to those who can handle jank and like slow, tedious experiences. This game is janky. Rough. I can see the seams between assets. Sound effects cut out when you get near the end of the game. Some things even lack sound. Encounters and balance goes from interesting and brutally fair to boring and grindy. Many bosses are good ideas executed poorly. In fact, that is what I'd say this game is: Great Ideas, Executed Poorly. But I love it. It captures the vibe of the first Dark Souls better than the sequels do. It is clear that there was clever thought put into the layout and inter-connectivity of the map, into the skills, into what enemies do and how they are supposed to act, and into some of the characters and weapons. This game fills a very specific niche for me that I thoroughly enjoy. The map slowly unfolds and you become familiar with locations and bosses. You want to keep the number of enemies you kill down to a minimum, about 50 for every boss you kill. Bosses you want to kill not just to get places but for the special currency they drop and the guaranteed rare drop. What this all means is you very quickly start plotting a path in your head of where you're going, what you're looking to get, and so on. Do I tackle the Rat King after Amara or go straight for the Gorewarden and Headmaster instead? Do I need to hit the merchant after Rat King or Astromancer's tower or can I skip them for the one in the chapel? Plotting and executing the route on the fly is very fun. The game is also very generous to how you can force builds, which is a plus for its format. It basically feels like a condensed version of dark souls, in which your rewarded for playing through multiple times and trying new builds. Whereas playing through dark souls is a very time demanding, long event, you can finish a run in this game in a little under an hour. The static map is to its benefit, but I really enjoy the very few times the enemy positions are different. Please more of this, and keep it character dependent. Also more things like the Ritters for the Archon where you're given multiple choices (Ignore, Kill, or Hire?), that change what you want to do depending on your setup. Running decay? Ignore the Ritter in the basement. Bad run? Hire or kill all the Ritters. God run? Just rush the Archon. This mid run decisions in a static map is very interesting. Imagine if Gorewarden and Istwan had similar things where you can destroy magical nexus or parades of students to depower Gorewarden, or prefight cut off Istwan's ability to resurrect his troops? I also wish more character's had as much thought put into them as the Astromancer and Animal Whisperer. They have more going for them that the other character's don't have. I'd actually like to see all the character's get redone in ways that they'll be more engaging. The devs have shown they are good with ideas already, so I'll not offer any, but what they have on these two characters I'd like to point out. -The dogs uniquely effect your play style and seem to scale with most stats. -The Astromancer's active ability is fun, odd he is the only one with an active ability. -Unique leveling every 5 levels for the Animal Whisperer is a dopamine rush. Lastly, I wish to point out my hate of unlocking skills I wish I could have used in a run by doing a run I wish I had those skills in. Want to unlock the Astromancer skills? Play through with the only one you have unlocked to unlock another one. Then play through with those two to unlock the other one, and finally again for the last one. Oh, what do you mean you don't want to do a fifth run in a row with astromancer skills to try the new ones? Overall, clunky, rough game, good ideas that are good enough I'll continue to play. Please devs, fix the sound at least.

This is an early access review, and my opinion may change with updates. The premise and formula for a good game is there currently, but the flaws are burnout inducing. Enemies can you hit you through buildings, and throw explosives across the map. Blocking is hit or miss, and healing is barely an option. The meta progression is interesting but not enough of a gameplay change for me to feel like my character is getting stronger between runs. It definitely doesn’t feel like progress is being made when you need to spend 15-20 minutes leveling from one when you die, meaning you often have to do full clears of content to gain levels and gear better than starting gear in the areas you’ve already cleared a hundred times just to make boss battles feasible. It has potential, but comes with more frustration than any feelings of achievement

Was this game made just for me? Seriously, it feels like this developer invaded my dreams and then created the perfect combination of games I love. It has no right being as good as it is. The best way to sum it up: Dark Souls 1 + Diablo + Halls of Torment mixed with Hardcore (1 life) and roguelike/roguelite elements. Also, they implemented a genius way to circumvent item bloat - when you pick up a new item, they ask you if you want to replace your old gear or not, and depending on which item you choose, the item not chosen automatically gets turned into gold. They even nailed the class fantasy for each class and I love jumping into a new game to try to make a certain build work. I'm calling it now. In a few years time, we will have a new genre of games called Hereticalikes. Can't wait to see what they keep doing with this gem.

Maybe I played too few, but I didn't get where's the roguelike mechanic? I'm dead, I restarted, everything was the same. The only difference, I already known part of the map, and I already known some prophecies, which technically are achievements. That doesn't make a roguelike, those are just base mechanics of a game (earnich achievements and memorizing the map between a run and another are cross-genre mechanics, not specific to any one genre). Roguelike is a game where you have a progression between runs. The next run should potentially not start in the same condition than the runs that preceded it. Expecially after the very first run, it should be evident to the player what they have to expect by the roguelike mechanic between a run and another. So the player knowns what should push him to try again. In general, I liked the effort in creating a soul-like feeling setting and mood. But I think you can't really apply soul-like fighting (z-targeting, even if performed by pointing the mouse, + dodge + parry) to an isometric low poly game. The low poly itself is the very first thing that ruins the game. As soon as it started I said "Oh no! It's a low poly one!". Then you find you should also understand what the enemy is doing, to be able to react in a "skill-based" way with parry or dodge... really? Into an isometric low poly game? You can't really say you can understand what's happening when you're surrounded by enemies. Maybe the things one you can "read" are ranged and area attacks. Why didn't they adopt a fighting more similar to the best action isometric games around, like Diablo? Why it had to be inspired to souls games (which are third person games, a whole different gameplay)? So, to my opinion, the idea of a roguelike isometric actionRPG is totally wasted away by adopting the wrong fighting system and a low poly graphic style. Somebody wrote "Dark Sould + Diablo" to justify its thumb up. You know, two good stuffs don't forcely make a better one. Choccolate and fried chickens are not a better plate. So "Dark Sould + Diablo" for me is a valid thumb down motivation, it's a bad idea. Because what I saw is the worse of Dark Souls + the worse of Diablo. They make a pair which doesn't work for me. Still, I'd be very curious to understand where's the roguelike mechanic. Maybe later in the game? But later is too late, should be clear immediately after the first death.

纯傻逼游戏，怪数值太高，玩家人数数值太低还没有恢复手段（除了2个血瓶），近战基本一直在掉血但是没有回血无限死，远程还能玩一玩靠走位躲闪攻击再堆高伤害总能通关。 虽然作者说每一局都体验不同，但是解决问题的思路很难改变，所以每一句的体验其实是差不多的。原因在于玩家构筑的速度跟不上膨胀的敌人数值，且玩家非常缺乏恢复手段但是很难避免伤害。 总之游戏难度太高，地图太小，战损太多缺乏恢复，非常不建议入手(就算是打折)，而且作者跑路了.... 补充一下，借用全解锁存档后明白了这是一个解锁的游戏，只要你吧预言都解锁了，你就能无压力的通关了。 总之这是一个局外养成大于局内的游戏，你是游玩体验核心在于局外解锁而不是局内通关，这很本末倒置。
